title: Ultra-high resolution structural and molecular imaging of cells and tissues
text:
Public Health Relevance/Narrative
Fluorescence microscopy is an increasingly critical tool in biomedical research. The proposed research seeks
to advance public health by allowing direct visualization at the nanoscale of molecular targets within live cells
and tissues and thus fostering new insights into a range of biomedical processes and mechanisms. Reflecting
NIH’s core mission, these efforts will support the development of fundamental knowledge that enhances
human health.

title: Evaluating the Impact of AI on Breast Cancer Screening Quality and Effectiveness: A Prospective RCT
text:
Screening mammography accuracy is limited by imperfect human interpretation, and prior computer-aided
detection (CAD) tools failed to improve performance. New AI CAD technologies show promise, but critical
knowledge gaps remain for key stakeholders regarding their benefits and harms. We propose a
groundbreaking, prospective randomized clinical trial to compare screening outcomes of 3D mammogram
interpretation with vs. without an FDA-cleared AI tool in clinical U.S. settings.

title: Multi-omic evaluation of atherogenic and non-atherogenic mechanisms and risk in calcific aortic valve disease
text:
PROJECT NARRATIVE / PUBLIC HEALTH RELEVANCE
Aortic stenosis is the most common valvular heart disease, impacting approximately 13 million individuals
worldwide, but has no effective medical therapy. Approximately half of individuals with aortic stenosis have
concomitant atherosclerosis (atherogenic aortic stenosis), however standard therapies targeting atherosclerosis
are not effective in preventing progression or reversing aortic valve pathology. This research proposal will
leverage clinical and molecular data to evaluate the underlying biology and associated clinical risk differentiating
atherogenic and non-atherogenic aortic stenosis, providing opportunity to advance the identification of novel
treatment targets and more personalized risk surveillance for individuals with this common disease.

title: Using Momentary Measures to Understand Physical Activity Adoption and Maintenance among Pacific Islanders in the United States
text:
NARRATIVE/PUBLIC HEALTH RELEVANCE
This project will examine the influences of neighborhood built and social environments, acute individual and contextual precipitants, as well as demographics and social history, biobehavioral and psychosocial predispositions on physical activity (PA) adoption and maintenance among sedentary Pacific Islander adults in Utah. The study will fill key gaps in the literature on important correlates and mechanisms underlying PA behavioral change for this fast-growing, high health risk, yet severely understudied population group, and will provide critical information on how to improve their PA level and reduce obesity and obesity-related health problems. The methodology and findings derived from this study will also provide a new perspective in understanding PA behavior of other racial/ethnic groups with high obesity and low PA levels.

title: Trans Nasal Transesophageal Echocardiography
text:
Transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) is an essential diagnostic tool in the assessment of heart structure
and function. TEE requires the use of sedation. Sedation requires specialized procedural space and skilled
providers, which increases procedural cost, burdens the workflow, increases the risk to the patient, and overall
limits the availability of TEE. Sedation accounts for the majority of the harm associated with TEE including
cardiovascular (hypotension, arrythmia) and respiratory compromise. We are designing, building, and testing a
novel trans-nasal TEE system that requires no anesthesia, which ultimately will improve safety, reduce cost,
and will expand availability.

title: Subtyping tinnitus based on fMRI dynamic functional connectivity
text:
Subjective tinnitus, defined as perceiving sound in the absence of actual sound affects 10% to
30% of the world population and at least half of tinnitus patients experience comorbidities such
as cognitive dysfunction, or depression. This study aims to identify subtypes of tinnitus using
state-of-the art neuroimaging, brain connectivity and machine learning methods. Subtyping
tinnitus based on dynamic functional connectivity of brain networks would allow more objective,
accurate and specific diagnosis, thus being an important step towards personalized tinnitus
treatment.

title: Project 3: Contribution of inflammation and DNA damaging factors to clonal expansion and malignant transformation in a community cohort of older adults
text:
As a complement to experimental mouse models in Projects 1 and 2, the human Project in the P01 Project 3 is
designed to identify modifiable risk factors for clonal expansion and malignant transformation in an epidemiologic
study. Identifying common, modifiable factors that drive clonal expansion and further transformation to
hematologic malignancy is closely aligned with the mission of the NCI, as it will provide opportunities to intercept
clonal expansion and malignant transformation and enable increased screening and early detection of clonal
hematopoiesis in persons at higher risk of hematologic malignancy due to their combined genetic and modifiable
risk factor profile.

title: BLOOD-BASED PROTEOMIC ASSAY FOR PANCREATIC CANCER DETECTION
text:
Detection of pancreatic cancer at early stages (when curable treatments are effective) could represent an
effective strategy to improve the survival rate of pancreatic cancer. Our prior studies have established blood-
based proteomic assays that showed high accuracy in detecting pancreatic cancer from healthy and benign
disease controls in multiple independent cohorts. The current proposal will carry out analytical and clinical
validations of the proteomic assays, which could be potentially deployed for clinical utilities if successfully
validated.

title: Single-cell immune landscape in the oral dysplasia's malignant transformation
text:
Prognostic biomarkers are critically needed to determine patients with oral dysplastic lesions at risk for
malignant transformation. We propose an innovative approach that combines high-dimensional imaging
mass cytometry (IMC) and machine learning predictive modeling (iEN) to analyze a total of ~200
Formalin-Fixed Paraffin-Embedded (FFPE) patient tongue biopsies from the Oral Pathology Archive at
the University of the Pacific (UOP), Arthur A. Dugoni School of Dentistry. Our goal is to establish a single-
cell atlas of premalignant immune microenvironment in oral dysplasia and to identify immune features
that predict the malignant transformation to oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma (OCSCC).

title: Construction and Application of Comprehensive Knowledge Graphs for Alzheimer's Disease
text:
We propose to use large-scale data, such as the Alzheimer's Disease Sequencing Project (ADSP), systematically collected
clinical and imaging data, and observations in the scientific literature, to identify factors that increase the risk of and
protection against dementia. Motivated by the great success of knowledge graph (KG) as a cornerstone of almost all
successful cognitive systems in industry, we propose to construct a novel and comprehensive AD-related knowledge graph
(AD-KG) platform based on multiple curated resources, literature, and a large-scale AD-related database with multiple types
of high-dimensional data in different studies that have different missing-data patterns.

title: Deep-UV Microscopy for Real-Time Adequacy Analysis of Bone Marrow Aspirates
text:
Bone marrow aspirates are critical to the diagnosis, staging, and monitoring of hematologic conditions and
cancers (e.g., leukemia, aplastic anemia, sickle cell disease, and metastasis of solid tumors), but 8-50% of the
700,000 aspirations performed annually in the US are unsuccessful due to operator technique, dilution of the
sample by peripheral blood, or underlying pathology. Unsuccessful aspirate samples necessitate repeating the
procedure, yet assessing which samples are successful/unsuccessful (i.e., adequate/inadequate) remains a
clinical challenge and is often not done until many days after the initial procedure. Cellia will improve the quality
and reliability of bone marrow aspiration procedures and reduce delays in diagnosis and administration of
treatment by developing a point-of-care instrument for rapid, non-destructive sample adequacy assessment.

title: Computational and Experimental Models of Myosin Variants
text:
A major challenge in understanding genetic based cardiac diseases is determining how single amino acid
changes in individual proteins scale from changes in structure to changes in function of muscle cells. We will
use structure-based computational platform that scales these levels and validate this testing platform with
experimental data primarily from stem cell derived cardiac muscle cells at the protein and contractile organelle
levels. This new platform will provide better understanding of the variant effects and applied to variants of
unknown significance.

title: Investigating the role of nicotine and the NRLP3 Inflammasome in HIV-1-Associated CNS Inflammation
text:
HIV infection in the brain and nicotine use both contribute to neuroinflammation and neurodegeneration and
are associated with activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome in the CNS. This project aims to understand the
common and distinct pathways by which nicotine and HIV lead to the breakdown of the blood-brain barrier,
neuroinflammation, and neurodegeneration while addressing the clinically relevant problem of nicotine
exposure in people with HIV and facilitating the potential development of treatments for these patients.

title: Coagulation Factor XII Recruitment and Activation During Thrombus Formation
text:
Inhibition of coagulation factor XII (FXII) could be a transformative new approach to antithrombotic treatment that
decouples therapeutic efficacy from the risk of bleeding complications. This proposal will explore the molecular
mechanisms of FXII recruitment, activation, and propagation at the platelet surface. Elucidation of these
processes is essential to the development of novel anti-thrombotic therapeutics based on FXII blockade.

title: SCH: Next-Generation Multimodal Wearable Sensing and Integrative AI Systems for Precision COPD Risk Prediction and Clinical Decision Support
text:
RELEVANCE (See instructions):  
This project develops a wearable sensor and an AI-powered system that alerts patients and physicians to dangerous 
changes in breathing and the environment before a medical emergency occurs, with the potential to prevent 
hospitalizations, improve quality of life, and deliver equitable respiratory care to those who need it most — including 
minority and under-resourced communities currently underserved by existing tools. The platform is built with and for 
the communities it serves and is designed to have broad public health impact nationwide.

title: Spatial-omic derived glycoproteomic urine biomarkers of lupus nephritis treatment response
text:
This multi-PI project will expand and validate the feasibility of using N-glycan analysis of urine
and captured glycoproteins from urine as biomarkers of progression from systemic lupus
erythematosus to lupus nephritis, and treatment response in lupus nephritis patients. Patient
matched serum, urine, biopsy tissues and peripheral blood mononuclear cells from lupus
nephritis subjects will be molecularly evaluated to identify underlying mechanistic biomolecules
to expand biomarker and therapeutic target options.

title: iPGDAC, An Integrative Proteogenomic Data Analysis Center for CPTAC
text:
The Clinical Proteomic Tumor Analysis Consortium (CPTAC) seeks to expand the proteogenomic
approach developed during the past 10 years to more cancer types and to translational research focusing on
clinically relevant problems. This application proposes an integrative proteogenomic data analysis center
(iPGDAC) built on our established expertise and resources. The overarching goal of the iPGDAC is to accelerate
the translation of cancer proteogenomic data into better understanding of cancer biology and improved cancer
treatment.

title: Dendrite regulation by the mitochondrial kinase PINK1: Implications for PD/LBD
text:
PUBLIC HEALTH NARRATIVE.
Loss-of-function mutations in PTEN-induced kinase 1 (PINK1) contribute to a recessive form of Parkinson's
disease with early cognitive dysfunction. In the prior grant period, we discovered that loss of PINK1 results
in diminished numbers of dendritic spines, particularly the type of spine most closely associated with long-
term memory storage. We will determine whether mitochondrial transport into dendrites is impaired by loss
of PINK1, and how PINK1 activity regulates brain cell responses involved in learning and memory in
cultured mouse and human neurons. These studies will help identify new strategies to prevent or slow the
loss of brain cell function in Parkinson's disease and related neurodegenerative dementias.

title: A nanopore biosensor for leveling Mtb antigens in blood
text: Tuberculosis (TB) is the leading cause of death from infectious disease worldwide but can be challenging to diagnose due to the poor performance of current diagnostic tests, which require sputum or tissue biopsies that can be difficult to obtain in certain patient populations, including children. In this work, we propose to employ protein-based nanopore technology, which can recognize single peptide detection events to quantify two tuberculosis-specific biomarkers (CFP-10 and ESAT-6), to develop a portable diagnostic and treatment monitoring system for resource-limited areas. Based on our preliminary studies, we are confident that this diagnostic system will benefit the global tuberculosis control effort by improving early diagnosis and treatment monitoring of tuberculosis.
